requirement: Identify the governing public pair as NCT04111276/WIRB20191576: Protocol V1.1 dated 7 June 2019 with WIRB protocol-level approval 11 July 2019 and the separate analysis plan dated 11 July 2019; keep the reference plan annotation-only.

evidence.text: The cover prints protocol ID 20191576, WIRB protocol-level approval Jul 11, 2019, and the running header identifies V1.1 dated 6/7/2019.
The separate plan repeats the exact title, Richard Komistek and University of Tennessee and is dated July 11, 2019.

requirement: Describe a prospective single-group within-participant biomechanical study in adults with symptomatic unicompartmental knee osteoarthritis, with each participant observed during gait without and with an OA brace in one data-collection session.

evidence.text: The protocol enrolls participants with symptomatic unicompartmental OA and collects gait first without and then with the brace, with comparative analysis for each subject.

requirement: Define the target population using the protocol eligibility boundary: Colorado Joint Replacement patients with marked unicompartmental degenerative joint-space narrowing who can walk normally, speak English, consent and are not pregnant or lactating; exclude bilateral subjects.

evidence.text: The cover lists the recruitment population and inclusion/exclusion criteria, including no bilateral subjects, pregnancy/lactation, inability to walk, unwillingness to consent and non-English speaking.

requirement: State that there is no randomized arm allocation and that brace order is fixed by protocol as no brace followed by brace; do not describe the conditions as two independent randomized cohorts.

evidence.text: Each subject performs gait without an offloading brace and is then fitted with the Breg brace for the second gait condition.
The reference incorrectly says the statistical analysis will analyze two cohorts.

notes: The registry correctly represents a single-group study; the reference's cohort wording must not erase pairing.

requirement: Define medial femoral-condyle separation from the medial tibial plateau as the principal continuous biomechanical outcome measured in both brace conditions.

evidence.text: The objective and data section specify medial condylar separation from the medial tibial plateau for every subject with and without the brace.

requirement: Analyze the outcome at the five prespecified stance-phase instants: heel strike, 33% stance, mid-stance, 66% stance and toe-off, retaining the phase-specific observations rather than collapsing them without justification.

evidence.text: Successive images are captured at heel strike, 33% of stance, mid-stance, 66% of stance and toe-off.

requirement: Document the outcome derivation from distortion-corrected fluoroscopic frames using subject-specific femur/tibia models and 3D-to-2D registration, including units, sign convention, frame selection and rules for multiple usable trials.

evidence.text: The protocol describes subject-specific 3D bone models overlaid on fluoroscopic images and permits multiple activity trials to acquire usable images, but it does not give units or aggregation rules.

requirement: Use a primary analysis that directly estimates the within-participant brace-minus-no-brace contrast, such as a paired model or participant-level repeated-measures model; do not use an independent-samples Student t test, Welch ANOVA or Mann-Whitney test as the primary analysis.

evidence.text: The same subject supplies both brace and no-brace gait measurements and the protocol calls for comparative analysis for each subject.
The reference instead lists Student t, Welch ANOVA and Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney tests for two cohorts.

notes: The reference methods conflict with the physical pairing and are annotation evidence requiring correction, not protocol-only truth.

requirement: Prespecify how brace condition and stance phase enter one repeated-measures analysis, including participant effect, condition-by-phase interaction, covariance or correlation structure and the target overall and phase-specific contrasts.

evidence.text: Every participant contributes brace and no-brace values at five stance-phase instants, creating correlated condition-by-phase observations.

requirement: Apply distributional diagnostics to paired differences or model residuals, not to the two condition samples separately; replace Bartlett/Levene variance testing and independent-sample fallbacks with diagnostics and robust methods appropriate to paired repeated observations.

evidence.text: The reference calls for Shapiro-Wilk plus Bartlett and Levene tests to select among independent-sample procedures.
The protocol establishes that both conditions and all phase instants are observed within participant.

requirement: Define a robust paired sensitivity analysis, such as a paired permutation test or Wilcoxon signed-rank analysis of participant differences, and specify how ties, zeros and the five stance phases are handled.

evidence.text: The proposed nonnormal fallback is the unpaired Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney U test and gives no rules for ties, zeros or repeated phase observations.

requirement: Define the primary analysis set and participant attribution rules, including consented but unmeasured participants, failure to complete one condition, unusable fluoroscopy, brace-fitting failure, incomplete phase frames, repeated trials and withdrawal with or without permission to retain prior data.

evidence.text: The protocol permits multiple trials for usable images and lets withdrawing participants choose whether collected data may remain, but it supplies no analysis-set rules.

requirement: Define the brace-effect estimand with population, outcome variable, condition contrast, stance-phase summary and strategy for inability to complete gait, pain-related stopping, poor brace fit, protocol deviations and post-consent withdrawal.

evidence.text: The objective defines the brace comparison; participants may stop and may withdraw or request destruction of prior data, but no estimand strategy is given.

requirement: Specify missing-data and measurement-failure handling at participant, condition, trial and stance-frame levels, including the primary assumption, whether partial phase profiles remain usable and a sensitivity analysis for informative inability to complete a condition.

evidence.text: Multiple trials and five frames per condition are planned, but neither protocol nor reference gives missing-frame, failed-condition or partial-profile rules.

requirement: Declare an estimation-focused primary contrast or define the confirmatory family and multiplicity control across five stance phases and any overall versus phase-specific tests; do not apply alpha 0.05 independently to every variable and phase.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies five stance-phase comparisons without a hierarchy.
The reference applies alpha 0.05 to all statistical tests without multiplicity control.

requirement: If formal testing is retained, state that alpha 0.05 is two-sided, align it with the declared primary family and report the corresponding confidence level; otherwise label all p-values exploratory.

evidence.text: The plan gives a 95% confidence level and alpha 0.05 but does not state sidedness, family or success rule.

requirement: Report condition- and phase-specific summaries plus paired mean or median differences, direction of benefit and two-sided confidence intervals using small-sample inference; do not report p-values alone.

evidence.text: The objective is the amount of medial separation with versus without a brace across five phases.
The reference names tests and a confidence level but does not define effect estimates, intervals or reporting by phase.

requirement: Use the prospective target of 20 evaluable participants and planned enrollment up to 24 to allow for dropout; do not substitute registry actual enrollment of 23 as the prospective target.

evidence.text: The protocol says 20 subjects will be assessed and enrollment will increase to 24 to account for dropouts; locations likewise say all 20 or possibly 24 subjects.

notes: Registry actual N=23 is not prospective sample-size evidence.

requirement: State that the protocol supplies an attrition allowance but no power or precision calculation, and provide or explicitly waive a paired-effect precision rationale appropriate to an exploratory biomechanical study.
acceptable_values: paired-effect precision rationale or explicit exploratory waiver

evidence.text: The prospective 20/24 targets are stated without an effect size, paired standard deviation, power or precision calculation.

requirement: Prespecify descriptive baseline and disease-characteristic summaries and any justified adjustment for baseline severity, laterality, gait speed or brace-fit factors; do not select covariates by baseline significance tests.

evidence.text: Eligibility depends on marked unicompartmental narrowing and trial speed is participant-dependent, but the analysis plan gives no baseline summaries or covariate rules.

requirement: Summarize procedure tolerability and safety using participant denominators, including inability or pain-related stopping and any imaging incident or adverse event, while keeping the biomechanical endpoint separate from clinical safety claims.

evidence.text: Participants may rest or stop at pain, and the protocol details fluoroscopy/CT risks and incidental findings, but neither document specifies safety summaries.

requirement: Reconcile all language, tables and tests with the single-group paired design: label brace and no-brace as conditions, not cohorts, and ensure every method preserves participant and stance-phase correlation.

evidence.text: Each participant undergoes both conditions at five phase instants.
The reference inconsistently calls the observations two cohorts and lists unpaired tests.

requirement: Name validated analysis software and version and provide reproducible model, diagnostic and contrast specifications; JMP alone is insufficient without a version and paired/repeated implementation details.

evidence.text: The reference names JMP Statistical Discovery but gives no version and no paired or repeated-measures implementation.
